envelope.description: Add the optional configReconcile field to MaintenanceResult and pin the interface contract

body.title: Add the optional configReconcile field to MaintenanceResult and pin the interface contract
body.summary: Extend MaintenanceResult at src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:40-44 with an additive, optional summary field. The existing interface is all-`readonly`, which the LLD's schemaDiff omitted: declare it `readonly configReconcile?: { readonly changed: boolean; readonly filled: number; readonly repaired: number; readonly error?: string | undefined } | undefined` — optionality written explicitly per exactOptionalPropertyTypes. Counts only; per-key dot-path detail goes to onLog. No existing field changes meaning and UpdateOptions gains nothing. This task owns the seventh LLD contract-level subject (MaintenanceResult.configReconcile is optional and additive, existing field set and meanings unchanged), and discharges it with a real test rather than a build side effect: add a type-level contract fixture that pins the existing field names and types (ok: boolean, steps, error) and asserts configReconcile is optional, so a future retype of `ok` or `steps` fails the suite instead of passing silently. Check the single downstream reader (src/cli/services/index.ts:91 → src/cli/panes/DaemonPane.tsx) still compiles and renders unchanged.
acceptanceChecks: MaintenanceResult gains only the readonly optional configReconcile field; ok, steps and error are untouched in name, type and meaning

A committed type-level contract fixture pins the pre-existing MaintenanceResult field names and types and the optionality of configReconcile, and fails to compile if any existing field is renamed, retyped, or made required
The field and its nested members are readonly with `| undefined` written explicitly, and typecheck passes under exactOptionalPropertyTypes
UpdateOptions is unchanged — no new flag
src/cli/services/index.ts and src/cli/panes/DaemonPane.tsx compile unchanged and DaemonPane's rendering is unaffected
